title: Khadija Comforts Muhammad
text:
Khadija bint Khuwaylid was a wealthy merchant of Mecca. According to the early biography of Ibn Ishaq, she hired a young man named Muhammad to take her goods to Syria, was impressed by his honesty, and proposed marriage to him herself. Tradition says he was twenty-five and she was about forty.

Around 610, when Muhammad was forty, he used to retreat to a cave on Mount Hira, outside Mecca, to meditate. There, according to Islamic tradition, the angel Gabriel appeared to him and commanded him to recite. Muhammad came home shaking with fear. The account preserved in the hadith collection of al-Bukhari says he went to Khadija and asked her to cover him, and she wrapped him up until his fear left him. Then he told her what had happened and said he feared for himself.

Khadija answered that God would never disgrace him. She reminded him that he kept good relations with his family, helped the weak, gave to the poor, honored his guests and stood by those struck by misfortune. Then she took him to her cousin, Waraqa ibn Nawfal, an old Christian scholar, who told Muhammad that what had come to him was the same messenger that had come to Moses.

Khadija is remembered in Islam as the first person to believe in Muhammad's message. They remained married until her death in 619, which tradition calls the Year of Sorrow.
lesson: When someone we love is frightened, reminding them of who they are can give them the courage to go on. A spouse's faith can steady us at our weakest moment.
people: Khadija bint Khuwaylid, Muhammad, Waraqa ibn Nawfal
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation, hadith 3; Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah, trans. A. Guillaume
caveat: The account is traditional, and Khadija's age at marriage is reported differently by some early sources.
